correctness.rationale: For \(a>b+c>0\), the two independent Poisson zero counts give an exact worst-phase objective. A midpoint shift makes the design depend only on the shortest angular gap; \(x=\cos\phi\) converts the adversarial phase into a quadratic on [-1,1]. Direct vertex/endpoint minimization is global and includes \(z=\cos(2\theta)\le0\), equality and \(r\ge4\) boundaries. Strict concavity of the interior-vertex value and convexity of the endpoint value produce one low-ratio optimizer, one high-ratio optimizer, and exactly two at \(r=4(\sqrt2-1)\). The symbolic \(r=1\) and \(r=2\) examples and actual checker.py grid/exact checks agree; finite checks are not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Two harmonics are the smallest phase-aligned periodic extension capable of two daily signal peaks. Under phase uncertainty, the exact threshold \(r=4(\sqrt2-1)\) changes a robust two-visit detection plan discontinuously: a gap below one quarter-period switches to exactly one half-period. This is a motivated complete classification of a concrete effort-constrained ecological observation objective; it is not a mere optimization of a static quadratic or a rebranded mean-signal result. It supplies a falsifiable design benchmark and identifies why simple half-day spacing can be suboptimal, without claiming field calibration.
